rationale: Both candidates independently flag the trust_remote_code True→False default flip in config_factory.py, which maps to the one clearly-confirmed GT concern (author's own 'this looks like a bug' comment). X adds three additional distinct, well-grounded findings (error.error.code fragility, UNSUPPORTED_ROUTES being skipped in the else branch — which loosely echoes GT's 'audit other endpoints'/batched-completions concern, and cache-invalidation scope), each concisely stated with a concrete recommendation. Y restates essentially the same trust_remote_code finding five times with near-identical evidence, padding the report without adding distinct value, and only contributes one genuinely new finding (unguarded load_deploy_config) beyond that. Neither review touches several real GT concerns (hf_config mutability/caching semantics, positional-arg signature risk, create_error_response reuse, debug-message scope, 500-error exposure to users), so recall is modest for both. X is more efficient, diverse, and actionable, while Y's redundancy meaningfully drags down its effective precision.
